thread:
Alyssa: Quick heads-up from Leo (reseller) — they expect a concentrated EU marketplace promotion for ~3 weeks starting mid-July, could be a 4–6x traffic multiplier for some image-to-text and embedding workloads. Asking if we can do a planned capacity swap to prioritize their listings.
Martin: Can you share rough GPU-hour estimate? 4–6x is vague, need baseline QPS and 99p latency targets.
Alyssa: Leo sent this: 'baseline 150 GPU-hours/day across eu-west-1 for the last month, promo peak could push to 700–900 GPU-hours/day for ~18 days. Target latency 120–200ms 99p.'
Samir: OK rough math: baseline 150 -> peak 800 -> +650 GPU-hours/day. For 18 days that's ~11.7k extra GPU-hours. Assuming P4d-like SKUs in our Dedicated fleet pricing that's a material uptick.
Rachel: Finance note — if we move capacity from other regions we'll need to track egress/cross-region transfer costs. Also, reserved commitments already pegged for Q3; any swap could affect unit economics.
Martin: Cluster constraints: eu-west-1 has two availability pools with limited spare racks. We can do one of three options: pre-warm instances (reserve temporary racks), shift lower-priority partners to us-west, or route some traffic to quantized model variants to reduce GPU usage.
Alyssa: Leo prefers single-region routing for compliance reasons, so cross-region fallback is not ideal. They asked for a playbook with minimal customer-visible regressions.
Samir: Proposal A (preferred): pre-warm 10 nodes (8x A40 equiv) for 3 weeks and enable aggressive batching + prefix cache. That should cover ~600–900 GPU-hrs/day. We also suggest a model variant (int8) for embeddings to cut unit hours ~1.6x.
Martin: Operational checklist:
```
- add 10 pre-warm nodes to eu-west-1 (label: reseller-q3-burst)
- autoscale policy: min=2,max=12,scale_metric=util
- enable prefix KV cache for reseller routes
- schedule canary in 3 steps (5%,25%,100%)
```
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: infra/prewarm-job queued for 2026-07-10T03:00Z (ETA 45m) :gear:
Rachel: Cost tradeoffs — pre-warm + reserved short-term likely cheaper than burst on spot or emergency on-demand. Estimate incremental cost for 18 days: ~$175k (including k8s overhead, storage, egress buffer). I'll do a detailed delta and attach a sheet after this thread.
Alyssa: Can infra confirm SLA/latency risk with model variant? We need to promise 99p latencies.
Martin: int8 variant shows 10–18% lower latency in perf tests, but tail can be noisy — we must keep a canary + fallback to fp16. We'll pin rollout to reseller route with failover.
Samir: Action items: 1) Martin to carve pre-warm plan + run dry-run perf tests by EOD tomorrow. 2) Rachel to finalize cost delta + approval threshold. 3) Alyssa to get Leo to sign a 3-week commit and clarify compliance constraints (no cross-region). 4) Ops to schedule pre-warm job and canary windows.
Martin: Also adding a note — if internal clusters hit network egress peaks, we may throttle non-critical background batch jobs (retrain/eval) during the window. Will coordinate with eng-ml.
Alyssa: Sounds good. Leo — can you confirm commit and whether they want a buyout for reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go?
leo_partner: We can commit to a 3-week purchase for priority listing placement. Prefer a short-term reserved rate if available. Compliance requires eu-west only.
Rachel: On receipt of commitment, I'll produce two pricing options: reserved short-term vs usage-based with a premium. We'll include a buffer for cross-region fallback (if needed) but mark it disallowed unless cleared.
Samir: I'll prepare a quick capacity ledger so we can reconcile after the promo. Expecting to relay nightly GPU-hour burn to partnerships channel.
Alyssa: Thanks team — if infra gives green tomorrow we'll lock dates and push the pre-warm. :thumbsup:
